newsitem.title: UK: Organisers cancel Islamic rally in London.
newsitem.headline: Organisers cancel Islamic rally in London.

text.p: An Islamic fundamentalist group, hit by increased security costs, on Friday cancelled a planned "Rally for Revival" that had triggered protests from Arab government because it featured militant Islamic leaders.
Representatives of al-Muhajiroun, a group calling for a holy war against governments in the Middle East, phoned the venue where the rally was set to be held on Sunday to call it off.

"Organisers rang to say they were unable to meet the hire cost of the building including additional security as a result of the publicity (surrounding the event)," Alex McCrindle, manager of the 12,000 seat London Arena, told Reuters.
The cancellation came just two days after the British government issued a stern warning to the organisers that it would not tolerate statements supporting terrorism.

Egypt and Algeria, which are both fighting internal Islamic threats, had urged Britain to ban the gathering. But a government spokesman said neither the Home Office nor the police had any powers to cancel the event.
Moslem academics and representatives from Islamic movements around the world had planned to attend the one-day rally.

Militant Islamic leaders including Omar Abdul-Rahman, the 65-year-old sheikh who was jailed for life for his part in the bombing of the World Trade Centre in New York, were also due to address the conference in pre-recorded videos.
McCrindle refused to divulge the exact amount of the additional security but said it involved thousands of pounds. He denied there were any political reasons behind the move.

"We weren't under any political pressure to cancel," he said. The founder of al Muhajiroun, militant Syrian Omar Bakri Mohammed who has called for a worldwide Islamic state, was not available to comment.
